problem_text:
A city planner must allocate the annual budget across 20 public infrastructure projects to maximize overall community benefit.  
Each project has the following characteristics:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.198, environmental impact 0.161, allocation limits [0.055, 0.459]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.156, environmental impact 0.251, allocation limits [0.044, 0.391]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.186, environmental impact 0.096, allocation limits [0.067, 0.788]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.140, environmental impact 0.042, allocation limits [0.061, 0.740]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.045, environmental impact 0.215, allocation limits [0.027, 0.470]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.057, environmental impact 0.255, allocation limits [0.080, 0.419]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.171, environmental impact 0.139, allocation limits [0.038, 0.826]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.156, environmental impact 0.135, allocation limits [0.081, 0.870]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.025, environmental impact 0.086, allocation limits [0.069, 0.814]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.182, environmental impact 0.261, allocation limits [0.028, 0.750]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.193, environmental impact 0.298, allocation limits [0.073, 0.302]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.117, environmental impact 0.222, allocation limits [0.057, 0.340]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.164, environmental impact 0.044, allocation limits [0.076, 0.635]  
* Project N: benefit score 0.021, environmental impact 0.113, allocation limits [0.003, 0.425]  
* Project O: benefit score 0.170, environmental impact 0.033, allocation limits [0.055, 0.407]  
* Project P: benefit score 0.025, environmental impact 0.240, allocation limits [0.001, 0.551]  
* Project Q: benefit score 0.057, environmental impact 0.221, allocation limits [0.012, 0.458]  
* Project R: benefit score 0.190, environmental impact 0.105, allocation limits [0.033, 0.528]  
* Project S: benefit score 0.123, environmental impact 0.157, allocation limits [0.082, 0.650]  
* Project T: benefit score 0.152, environmental impact 0.090, allocation limits [0.058, 0.683]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified limits, and the total allocation across all projects must equal the full budget (sum to 1). To prioritize essential services, the subset of high-priority projects L = {A, B, C, F, G, H, J, K, M, N, O, P, Q, R, S, T} must together receive at least 0.785 of the total budget. Additionally, the total environmental impact of all selected projects must not exceed 0.205, and the overall benefit score must be at least 0.126. Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes total community benefit while satisfying all constraints.
